## History

The line of descent, oldest first:

- **the bronze dragon proto-language**, 20 kyr ago: the reconstructed ancestor (bronze dragon).
- **Na sheþivi (bronze dragon 8, the south of Simath)**, 20 kyr ago: continued the proto-language in place (spoken by bronze dragon).
- **Nateeitei (fire giant 3, the south-west of Simath)**, 10 kyr ago: formed when the speakers took up another language.

| | consonants | vowels | tones |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the bronze dragon proto-language, 20 kyr ago | 10: n t d k ɡ kʰ ɗ ts j r | 6: i iː e a a‼ aː | none |
| now | 8: n t k dʒ s ʁ h j | 5: i e ɛː a a‼ | none |

**Shift.** 10 kyr ago the fire giant speakers of deme 196 took up the language of the bronze dragon (bronze dragon 8). Trigger: trade: the fire_giant and bronze_dragon shared land from 20.0 to 0.0 kyr ago (presence table).
From the old language (fire giant 3) 56 words were kept, mostly landscape, plants and animals: fish, fly (insect), bird, dog, flower, leaf, louse, root, stone or rock, worm, deer, grass, land, sea, ….
The accent the speakers brought (new sound heard as old): dz > z, kʰ > k, v > x, ɗ > t, ʒ > dʒ, ʔ > h.
Grammar carried over: definite article none > post; perfective none > marked.

**Contact.** Sound changes taken up from neighbours by the wave along the line: kenku 2 (11), goliath 1 (10), kobold 10 (9), tortle 2 (9), lizardfolk 1 (5), kenku 10 (5). Loan events in the present vocabulary (by donor): goliath 1 (12), bronze dragon 8 (10), copper dragon 5 (9), brass dragon 5 (8), silver dragon 10 (8), kobold 102 (7).

## Orthography

The house romanization in two registers: the full spelling (workbench, one letter or digraph per sound, tone marks) and the book spelling (lossy: no tone, plain vowels, at most one diacritic letter a word).

**Vowels:** i ‹i› · e ‹e› · ɛː ‹èe› ‹ee› · a ‹a› · a‼ ‹arh›

Where two spellings are given the second is the book spelling.

## Grammar

Basic word order is SVO; it has prepositions. In the noun phrase: possessed before the possessor; noun before the adjective; noun before the demonstrative; numeral before the noun; noun before the relative clause. Overall it is head-initial.
It has a definite article after the noun, an indefinite article, no case marking on nouns, no alignment marking (subject and object are not told apart by form), singular and plural, no gender or noun classes.
Verbs mark past; there are no evidentials. Negation uses a negator before the verb; yes/no questions use a final question particle. Verbs do not agree with their arguments.
Other features: pronouns can be dropped; serial verbs; verb reduplication; a copula; a periphrastic causative; no passive; question words left in place; a decimal counting base.
Measured morphology: 8 live grammatical markers, mean bondedness 0.2 (0 free word … 3 fused), 0 paradigm cells, 0 of them with allomorphy.

### Grammar sketch

Built from the typology and the live markers above (planet/language/sentences.py); where the engine tracks no marker for a construction, the form is the word such markers commonly grow from, and the text says so. Examples are glossed by the Leipzig rules (abbreviations under Sample sentences).

**Number.** Nouns mark number: plural: a clitic before the noun (na, from 'all').

| *neji* |
| --- |
| dog |

‘dog’

| *na=neji* |
| --- |
| PL=dog |

‘dogs’

**Case.** Nouns have no case marking. Subject and object are not marked apart: word order tells them. Place and company are said with the plain words 'in' (hɛːhe), 'at' (dʒitina), 'with' (hihɛːei) as adpositions.

**Gender and noun classes.** There is no gender or noun class.

**Tense and aspect.** Verbs mark tense and aspect. Past (PST): a separate word before the verb (hihɛː, from the perfect marker). Unmarked: future, perfective, progressive, habitual (left to context).

| *hihɛː* | *ta‼* |
| --- | --- |
| PST | go |

‘(it) went’

**Mood and evidentiality.** No evidential or mood marker is live; statements are unmarked.

**Person agreement.** Verbs do not agree with the subject. Pronoun-like words stand beside the verb (2SG dʒeja, 1PL hɛːa), on their way to becoming agreement.

**Negation.** Negation uses the word for 'not' (hita), preverbal.

| *a‼hi* | *hita* | *ita* | *hei* | *nɛːhi* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1SG | NEG | drink | water | DEF |

‘I do not drink the water.’ (sentence 6 below)

**Questions.** Yes/no questions use a particle at the end of the clause. Question words stay where the questioned phrase would stand: who hahe, what hiha‼i, where hiha‼ita, when hiha‼ta, how ka.

### Families a speaker feels

The roots a speaker still feels: a derivation or compound younger than 3 kyr whose parts are still in use (per-word `roots`). 3 families of 3+ words; 21% of the 365 words share a root with another word.

The largest: **water** *ɡeɡ* (N, coined 20 kyr ago in the bronze dragon proto-language); 4 words have it as their main root, 4 contain it.

| milk | heje | heye | water, breast | \*ɡeɡ 'water' (the bronze dragon proto-language, 20 kyr) → WATER + BREAST = 'milk' (0.5) |

## Sample sentences

Built from this language's own words, word order, markers and agreement (planet/language/sentences.py). Each has the form line (‘-’ an affix boundary, ‘=’ a clitic boundary), a morpheme-by-morpheme gloss, the free translation, then the whole sentence in IPA (after the simple joining rules: a glide between two vowels, a nasal taking the place of a following stop) and in the book spelling. Nothing here is attested speech; it is what the grammar data implies.
